Add z-scores to growth data

Source: R/ref-zscores.R
wgh_add_zscores.Rd

Adds height-for-age (haz), weight-for-age (waz) and BMI-for-age (baz) z-scores against the chosen reference. Under the WHO reference weight-for-age is only defined up to 10 years and is NA above that age. The CDC 2000 charts cover 2 to 20 years.

Usage

wgh_add_zscores(
  x,
  indicators = c("haz", "waz", "baz"),
  reference = "who",
  method = c("who", "lms", "symmetric"),
  flag_limit = 6,
  percentiles = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A wgh_data object or data frame with age, sex and the needed measurements (height, weight, bmi).

indicators

Which z-scores to add.

reference

"who" (default), "cdc" or a custom LMS table.

method

See wgh_zscore(). Use "lms" or "symmetric" only to reproduce earlier results computed that way.

flag_limit

Absolute z-score at or above which a value is flagged as biologically implausible in a column <z>_flag. Use NULL for no flags.

percentiles

Also add percentile columns (haz_pct, ...).

Value

x with the z-score columns (and flags) added, in the same container type as x.

Next steps

Classify nutritional status with wgh_classify(), summarise with wgh_prevalence(), or plot individual children with wgh_plot_growth_chart().

Examples

gd <- wgh_add_zscores(growdat)
summary(gd$haz)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> -5.0816 -0.3882  0.1924  0.2096  0.7905  5.6703 
# CDC 2000 references with percentiles
cdc <- wgh_add_zscores(growdat[growdat$age >= 2, ], reference = "cdc", percentiles = TRUE)
head(cdc[, c("age", "height", "haz", "haz_pct")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>     age height    haz haz_pct
#>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1  3.00    95  0.270     60.7
#> 2  3.90   103. 0.693     75.6
#> 3  6.13   117. 0.248     59.8
#> 4  7.10   123. 0.122     54.9
#> 5  8.09   129. 0.0850    53.4
#> 6  9.00   134. 0.221     58.8
